VR.1.1.1.note: Third review, vyākhyā only (new §5.4). Correct as it stands. Rule 1: connected prose, no dash chains. Rule 2: every word boundary checked by hand; no external sandhi (तपस्वी इति उच्यते, सम्यक् जानतां), anusvāra only before consonants, म् before vowel and pause (वाग्विदाम् इत्युक्ते, जनानाम् ;). Rule 3: यः … सः (यः मुनिषु श्रेष्ठः सः मुनिपुङ्गवः), अतः, किञ्च, इति आशयः, all used correctly. Rule 4: स्वाध्यायः इत्युक्ते वेदस्य पठनम् (nominative with nominative), वाग्विदाम् इत्युक्ते … जनानाम् (genitive with genitive), परिपप्रच्छ, इत्युक्ते प्रश्नं पृष्टवान् are all right. Rule 5: two stretching constructions, the finite passive उच्यते and the present participle जानताम्. (Following the owner's sample I do not count the fixed इत्युक्ते, nor क्त/क्तवतु forms such as पृष्टवान्.) Rule 6: no compound but the verse's own. Rule 7: all eight significant padas in bold (the long compound through तपसि, स्वाध्याये, निरतः); 5 sentences; nothing added beyond the verse. On the connective inference सः सदा तपः करोति स्म, अतः तपस्वी इति उच्यते: this is the meaning of तपस्वी put as a sentence and is acceptable. OPTIONAL: सदा is slightly more than the word says of Vālmīki (the verse has निरत only of Nārada, and the padārtha has plain तपः कुर्वन्); it can be dropped. The explanation स्वाध्यायः इत्युक्ते वेदस्य पठनम् hangs on a comma after आसीत्; a semicolon, as elsewhere, would read better.

VR.1.1.2.note: Correct as it stands. Rule 1: connected prose. Rule 2: all boundaries clean (साम्प्रतम् अस्मिन्, कृतम् उपकारं स्मरन् पुरुषः, कदाचित् अपि, इदानीं लोके); no anusvāra before a vowel or pause. Rule 3: यः … सः three times and यस्य … सः, correlatives matched; किञ्च; the closing इति वाल्मीकेः प्रश्नस्य आशयः gathers the questions well. Rule 4: साम्प्रतम् इत्युक्ते इदानीम्; … स्मरन् पुरुषः कृतज्ञः इति उच्यते; the explanations of धर्मज्ञः, सत्यवाक्यः and दृढव्रतः are correct and say no more than the words. Rule 5: two, the present participle स्मरन् and the finite passive उच्यते (कृतम् is a क्त form, not counted). Rule 6: only the verse's compounds. Rule 7: all significant padas bold; speaker named and linked to परिपप्रच्छ of verse 1; 5 sentences; nothing added. The two questions गुणवान् कः and कः च वीर्यवान् are joined into one (गुणवान् वीर्यवान् च कः अस्ति), which is harmless since all the questions seek one man, as the last sentence says. OPTIONAL: गुणवान् and वीर्यवान् are left to the padārtha; that is allowed.

VR.1.1.3.note: The vyākhyā itself is correct and needs no change; the flag only carries forward the standing points for the scholar (below). Rule 1: connected prose. Rule 2: boundaries clean (चारित्रम् इत्युक्ते शोभनम् आचरणम्, न अस्ति चेत् सः). Rule 3: यः … सः, यं … सः, and चेत् correctly placed at the end of its clause (तादृशः अन्यः न अस्ति चेत् सः …); तथा च, ततः, इति आशयः. Rule 4: चारित्रम् इत्युक्ते शोभनम् आचरणम् (both neuter nominative); यं दृष्ट्वा (सर्वे) जनाः प्रीताः भवन्ति सः प्रियदर्शनः is a correct explanation, and the last clause renders एकः = अद्वितीयः exactly as ruled, with (सर्वे) in brackets. Rule 5: two, the finite passive पृच्छ्यते and the gerund दृष्ट्वा. पृच्छ्यते is correctly formed (प्रच्छ् takes samprasāraṇa before यक्, 6.1.16); दृष्ट्वा has the same agent as प्रीताः भवन्ति, as it must. Rule 6: only the verse's compounds and its member प्रियदर्शनः. Rule 7: all significant padas bold; linked by पुनः, speaker named; 5 sentences; nothing added. STANDING POINTS FOR THE SCHOLAR, unchanged from the second review: (1) एकप्रियदर्शनः is read by the owner's ruling as एकः (अद्वितीयः) प्रियदर्शनः; the alternative, a bahuvrīhi एकम् (केवलम् / सदा) प्रियं दर्शनं यस्य सः, exists in the tradition and is recorded here only for completeness. (2) Linga still to be verified in the kośas (I am working from memory): चारित्र नपुं rests on Apte (चारित्रम्), I do not recall it in the Amarakośa; भूत in सर्वभूतेषु नपुं rests on Apte and on the constant usage सर्वाणि भूतानि, while the Amarakośa nānārtha line as I recall it (… भूतं प्राण्यतीते समे त्रिषु) gives the sense 'living being' without a fixed gender.

VR.1.1.4.note: Correct as it stands, and not a copy of the owner's sample (every explanation is worded differently). Rule 1: connected prose. Rule 2: boundaries clean (नारदम् अन्यत् अपि, तस्मात् भीताः, युद्धम् ;). Rule 3: यः … सः, यस्य … सः, यदा … तदा with matched correlatives; तथा च, किञ्च, इति आशयः. Rule 4: आत्मवान् इत्युक्ते स्वस्य मनसः स्वामी; यस्य तेजः अस्ति सः द्युतिमान्; यः अन्येषां गुणान् न निन्दति, ईर्ष्यां च न करोति, सः अनसूयकः इति उच्यते; संयुगः इत्युक्ते युद्धम् (संयुगः masculine as ruled) are all correct. The last sentence turns the epic genitive कस्य into the ablative तस्मात्, as the ruling requires. Rule 5: two, the gerund जित्वा (क्रोधं जित्वा वर्तते) and the finite passive उच्यते. Rule 6: only the verse's compounds. Rule 7: all significant padas bold; linked by अन्यत् अपि, speaker named; 6 sentences. On इति अन्तिमः प्रश्नः: it is true of the text (verse 5 asks nothing more) and matches the owner's own अन्ते वाल्मीकिः पृच्छति; acceptable as connective context. OPTIONAL: (a) in यदा सः पुरुषः युद्धे क्रुद्धः भवति … the सः has nothing before it to point to; युद्धे क्रुद्धात् यस्मात् देवाः अपि भीताः भवन्ति, सः कः इति आशयः is tighter. (b) तु in यः तु क्रोधं जित्वा वर्तते marks a contrast that is not there; च would be more exact.

VR.1.1.5.note: Correct as it stands. Rule 1: connected prose. Rule 2: boundaries clean (पृष्टं तत् एव अत्र एतत् इति, कारणम् अपि, कौतूहलम् अस्ति, एवंविधं नरं ज्ञातुं). Rule 3: यत् … तत्, यः … सः, अतएव, ततः, इति आशयः twice. Rule 4: कौतूहलम् इत्युक्ते ज्ञातुम् इच्छा, सा च महती इति आशयः explains कौतूहलम् and परम् together, with सा महती agreeing with इच्छा; यत् पूर्वं पृष्टं तत् एव अत्र एतत् इति उच्यते is a good way to explain the pronoun; सः कारणम् अपि वदति brings out हि. Rule 5: two, the gerund पृष्ट्वा and the finite passive उच्यते (पृष्टम् is a क्त form, not counted, as in the owner's sample). Rule 6: only the verse's compounds. Rule 7: all fourteen significant padas bold; linked by एवं प्रश्नान् पृष्ट्वा, speaker named; 5 sentences. On the inference नारदः तं ज्ञातुं शक्नोति, अतएव वाल्मीकिः नारदं पृच्छति इति आशयः: the verse says only that Nārada is able to know such a man; that this is why he is asked is the plain purpose of the line and is marked as आशयः, so it stays within connective context. The five vyākhyās read as one piece: verse 1 sets the scene, 2–4 open with पृच्छति / पुनः / अन्यत् अपि, 5 closes with एवं प्रश्नान् पृष्ट्वा.
